title: Reality of relative factors for an envelope
statement:
Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be as in [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual], and
let $\mathcal E$ be lisse, $\iota$-real, and punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight zero. Then every $R^ih_!\mathcal E$ is $\iota$-real.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal G_i=\mathcal H^i(Rh_!\mathcal E)$. These are constructible Weil sheaves: $h$ is separated of finite type and its source and target are separated of finite type over $k_0$, as required in [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual]. At a finite coefficient field, [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] puts the compact-support image of an integral representative in the completed integral constructible category. The rationalization and common-stage formulas of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] therefore put $Rh_!\mathcal E$ in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$. The lift [prop-weil-operations] supplies its Weil structure, and [prop-constructible-truncations] supplies constructible cohomology with that structure. Thus the pointwise reality condition of [def-wf-iota-real] applies to each $\mathcal G_i$; no lissity of a direct image is asserted.

source.place: first paragraph: define the local factors, including their constructible domain

proof.text: Fix a closed point $y\in Y_0$, write $m=[\kappa(y):k_0]$, $Q=q^m$, and put $C_0=U_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, $C=C_0\times_{\kappa(y)}k$. Write $\mathcal E_y$ for the restriction with Weil structure given by the $m$-fold iterate of that of $\mathcal E$. The fibre hypotheses in [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual] make $C_0$ a smooth affine curve of relative dimension one over $\kappa(y)$, possibly empty; separatedness and finite type also follow from [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Restricting an etale trivialization gives a trivialization of the pullback, so $\mathcal E_y$ is lisse by [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. By [lem-tw-punctual-rescaling] it is punctually pure of weight zero relative to $Q$.

source.place: first paragraph: the fibre and normalization by its residue cardinality

proof.text: The fibre inclusion $C_0\hookrightarrow U_0$ is a closed immersion (it is the inverse image of the closed point $y$). Clause 1 of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] identifies its closed-point stalks and their local operators when both schemes are viewed over $k_0$. For a closed $x\in C_0$ of degree $r$ over $\kappa(y)$, its degree over $k_0$ is $mr$. Over $\kappa(y)$ the local operator of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] uses $(\theta^{[m]})^{[r]}=\theta^{[mr]}$ and point transport by $\gamma^{mr}$, exactly the same formula as over $k_0$. Hence it is the same operator on the same stalk. Its characteristic polynomial is real by the hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ and [def-wf-iota-real]. This proves that $\mathcal E_y$ is real over $\kappa(y)$.

source.place: second paragraph: justify reality of the restricted sheaf and its local factors

proof.text:
Apply the compact-support base-change clause 4 of [prop-functor-package] to the geometric fibre square of $h$, on its $\Qlb$ bounded constructible domain. Evaluation at $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and degree-$i$ cohomology, as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], give an isomorphism
$$b_{i,y}:(\mathcal G_i)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i:=H_c^i(C,\mathcal E_y).$$
The base-change comparisons are equivariant by [prop-weil-operations]. In the local formula of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], $g_Y^m\bar y=\bar y g_s^m$; after this return, the same base-change comparison uses the restricted $m$-fold Weil map. Thus its equivariance says explicitly $b_{i,y}F_y=F_{C/\kappa(y)}b_{i,y}$, where the right-hand operator is the compact-support transport followed by that restricted Weil map of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. Consequently the local characteristic factor of $\mathcal G_i$ is
$$P_i(T):=\iota\det(1-TF_{C/\kappa(y)}\mid V_i),\qquad P_i(0)=1.$$

source.place: first paragraph: base change identifies the local factors with fibre factors

proof.text: Here are the finite-level hypotheses needed to apply the trace formula on $C_0$. By [def-wf-weil-category], the Weil sheaf has a finite coefficient-field representative $(E,(K_E,\theta_E))$. We may enlarge $E$ so that $K_E$ is a sheaf in degree zero: clause 3 of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] represents the two heart conditions at finite stages, and the common-stage morphism convention in [def-wf-weil-category] represents the required isomorphisms at a common finite extension. Since truncations commute with finite scalar extension by [prop-constructible-truncations], their vanishing and hence the two heart conditions hold at a sufficiently large common stage. The rational category has integral representatives, and [lem-trf-curve-integral-lattice], applied to $K_E$ on the separated affine curve $C_0$ of dimension at most one, supplies a lattice $M$ whose every derived reduction $M_n$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(C,A_{E,n})$ and has an explicit etale-origin witness. No integral or invertible-on-a-lattice Weil structure is being assumed.

source.place: second paragraph: discharge the coefficient hypotheses of the general trace formula

proof.text: Choose a compactification of $C_0\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ over $\kappa(y)$ by [thm-nagata-compactification]; the base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the curve is separated of finite type. All graph correspondences of the Frobenius iterates and their fixed-point base changes on its geometric compactification have separated finite-type source and target over $k$. The last paragraph of [def-trf-admissibility] states that exceptional admissibility on these constructible domains is a theorem for every such morphism. More explicitly, [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] supplies the relative adjunction and compactification comparisons on etale-origin inputs, and [thm-sf-preservation-class] supplies bounds uniform in the finite coefficient level, with separated targets as here. Together with the lattice witnesses in Step 5, these discharge exactly the finite-level hypotheses of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar], and therefore those of [thm-trf-l-function-euler-product].

source.place: second paragraph: discharge compactification admissibility for the trace formula

proof.text:
To apply degree-zero vanishing without assuming connected fibres, use [lem-zl-affine-geometric-components-finite-extension] over $\kappa(y)$: after a finite extension $\mathbf F_{Q^e}$, the curve decomposes into finitely many smooth geometrically connected affine curves $C_{a,e}$. By [lem-zl-weil-constant-extension-frobenius] the restriction of $\mathcal E_y$ to this extended base is lisse. Its restriction to each open and closed component is still lisse by the local definition [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Thus [lem-a1-affine-hc0] gives $H_c^0(C_a,\mathcal E_{a,e})=0$ for every component. Finite clopen decomposition [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] and exceptional restriction [lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction], with the constructible adjunction of [prop-functor-package], give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!\mathcal E_y,L)\cong\prod_a\operatorname{Hom}(R(a_a)_!\mathcal E_{a,e},L),$$
where $a:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_a:C_a\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. This is the universal property of the finite direct sum, so evaluation and degree-zero cohomology give $V_0=\bigoplus_a H_c^0(C_a,\mathcal E_{a,e})=0$. The underlying coefficient space is unchanged by the finite constant extension, as stated in [lem-zl-weil-constant-extension-frobenius]; only its Frobenius is replaced by an $e$-th power. The empty-family clause gives the same result for the empty fibre. Hence $P_0=1$.

source.place: first paragraph: justify degree-zero vanishing also on disconnected and empty fibres

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual] with weight zero and $i=1$ to the given $h,\mathcal E$. By the Frobenius-compatible identification of Step 4, every reciprocal root of $P_1$ has modulus at most $Q^{1/2}$. Step 2 supplies the hypotheses of [lem-zl-affine-curve-hc2-purity] over the finite field $\kappa(y)$, so every reciprocal root of $P_2$ has modulus $Q$. These are reciprocal roots (Frobenius eigenvalues), not roots in the variable $T$, whose moduli are their inverses. Finally [lem-zl-affine-curve-range], applied to the constructible sheaf $\mathcal E_y$ on the smooth affine curve $C_0$, gives $V_i=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$. Its statement explicitly includes disconnected and empty curves.

source.place: first paragraph and end of second paragraph: the reciprocal-root bounds and cohomological range

proof.text:
Apply clauses 2--4 of [thm-trf-l-function-euler-product] over $\kappa(y)$ to $\mathcal E_y$, using Steps 5--6 to supply its finite-level hypotheses. It gives
$$L_\iota(C_0,\mathcal E_y,T)=P_1(T)/P_2(T)\quad\text{in }\mathbf C[[T]],$$
since $P_0=1$. The cohomological operator is the global geometric Frobenius used in Step 4, as specified in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. The local Euler-product operators in that theorem agree up to conjugacy with the geometric-point operators of Step 3 by [lem-rp-local-frobenius-models-agree]; its required lattice with finite-Tor reductions was supplied in Step 5. Thus each local factor is real by Step 3. The Euler product is locally finite by clause 1 of [thm-trf-l-function-euler-product], so each coefficient uses finitely many factors and is real. Therefore the Taylor series of $P_1/P_2$ is in $\mathbf R[[T]]$.

source.place: second paragraph: coefficient trace formula and real Euler factors

proof.text:
Write $A=P_1$, $B=P_2$, and put a bar over coefficientwise complex conjugates. Since $A/B$ has real Taylor coefficients and $B(0)=1$, it has the same Taylor series as $\bar A/\bar B$. Multiplying by $B\bar B$ gives $A\bar B=\bar A B$ as polynomials. Thus both $A\bar B$ and $B\bar B$ have real coefficients, the latter is nonzero, and
$$A/B=(A\bar B)/(B\bar B)\in\mathbf R(T).$$
This supplies rational-function reality from series reality without assuming that real Taylor coefficients alone are a definition of $\mathbf R(T)$.

source.place: second paragraph: justify the implication from real Euler coefficients to a real rational function

proof.text: Here $Q\geq2$, so $Q^{1/2}<Q$. The reciprocal-root bounds of Step 8 and [lem-zl-root-radius-separation], with $R=Q^{1/2}$ and $S=Q$, say that all reciprocal roots of $P_2$ survive in the reduced denominator with their full multiplicities. Therefore $P_1$ and $P_2$ have no common root and are coprime. They both have constant coefficient one, and Step 10 gives $P_1/P_2\in\mathbf R(T)$. Apply [lem-zl-real-reduced-factors] to obtain $P_1,P_2\in\mathbf R[T]$. This argument also covers constant factors $P_1=1$ or $P_2=1$, since their reciprocal-root conditions are vacuous.

source.place: second paragraph: separated reciprocal radii and real normalized reduced factors

proof.text: Steps 7--8 give $P_i=1$ in every degree other than $1,2$, and Step 11 gives real coefficients in those two degrees. Step 4 identifies these with the local characteristic factors of $\mathcal G_i$ at $y$. The point $y$ was arbitrary and Step 1 supplied constructibility and the Weil structure. By [def-wf-iota-real], every $R^ih_!\mathcal E=\mathcal G_i$ is therefore $\iota$-real.

source.place: second paragraph: pointwise reality of all relative factors

proof_origin.place: both proof paragraphs, with coefficient domains, finite-stage hypotheses, fibre normalization, disconnected-fibre vanishing and rational descent made explicit
